literal: Than those who have renounced, purity they possess, transgressors' mouth harsh words those who can endure.
translation: Those who can endure harsh words from the mouths of transgressors possess a purity greater than that of ascetics.
modern: வரம்பு மீறியவர்களின் வாயிலிருந்து வரும் கடுமையான சொற்களைப் பொறுத்துக்கொள்பவர்கள், பற்றுகளைத் துறந்த முனிவர்களை விடவும் தூய்மையானவர்கள் ஆவார்கள்.
explanation: The couplet compares the virtue of patience with the purity of renunciation. It states that those who can patiently endure harsh words from people who transgress boundaries of decency are purer than ascetics who have renounced the world. The word 'இறந்தார்' refers to those who have crossed the limits of proper conduct, while 'நோற்கிற்பவர்' highlights the active strength required to bear their insults. Thus, true purity lies not just in leaving the world, but in maintaining one's composure amidst its provocations.
